Primary Care Progress Note
Date: 08/08/2026
Patient: Laurette Brown, 89-year-old female

Subjective:
Ms. Brown presents today for her routine follow-up. She reports feeling generally well with no new complaints. She denies any recent falls or injuries.

Objective:
Vital signs are stable. Physical examination reveals normal cardiovascular and respiratory function. Musculoskeletal exam shows no tenderness or deformity.

Assessment:
Ms. Brown remains in stable condition with no acute issues noted today.

Plan:
Continue current management and routine monitoring. Encourage regular physical activity and balanced nutrition. Follow up in 6 months or sooner if any concerns arise.

Radiology Report
Date: 08/31/2026
Patient: Laurette Brown, 89-year-old female

The lumbar spine radiograph shows changes at the L3 vertebral level. Approximately 30% loss of L3 vertebral body height. Focal kyphotic deformity at L3 measuring 28 degrees. No other abnormalities are identified in the examined spinal segments.

Impression:
Moderate compression fracture of the L3 vertebral body with focal kyphotic deformity as described. Clinical correlation is advised.

Spine Intervention Consultation
Date: 09/02/2026
Patient: Laurette Brown, 89-year-old female

History and Presentation:
Back pain began 07/30/2026 after bending to pick up a grandchild, 5 weeks before this visit. Pain NRS 5/10 despite 4 weeks of optimal non-surgical management with oxycodone 5 mg as needed, a thoracolumbar brace and activity modification. Pain has been stable to slightly improved since the fracture. Back pain localizes to the fractured level; afebrile with no signs of infection or discitis.

Clinical Course:
Seen in the outpatient spine clinic; not hospitalized for this fracture. Roland Morris Disability Questionnaire score 20/24.

Management:
Referred for DEXA bone density testing and osteoporosis education; enrolled in the osteoporosis treatment program.

Summary:
The patient presents with persistent but stable back pain following a vertebral fracture sustained 5 weeks ago. Current management includes pain control, bracing, and activity modification. Further evaluation and treatment for osteoporosis are underway to reduce future fracture risk.
